what_happened: The ego had drifted about 9 m left of the recorded path, into a left lane, even though the command was RIGHT. Bus 127 merged diagonally into that lane ahead and straightened out there. The ego slowed only gradually (7.3 to 3.4 m/s) and ran into the back of the slow bus; the rear contact recorded for this run came after this front collision.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded car stayed in the right lane, but the ego drifted about 9 m left into what appear to be oncoming lanes. Bus 127 came out of the intersection head-on in that lane and struck the ego's front. The ego was slowing (7.3 to 3.7 m/s) but never moved back out of the bus's path.

The route command was RIGHT, but the ego went the other way. It turned left across the multi-lane road, away from the route on the right, and slowly drove over the left edge of the road into the building frontage, where it went offroad at 10.2 s about 13 m from the recorded path. No other actors were involved. The camera view smears more as the ego gets further from the recorded path, but the wrong-way turn had already started before that.

With a RIGHT command, the ego drifted left and ended up about 8.6 m from the recorded path, in the leftmost lanes. Bus 127 turned in from the cross street into that lane heading toward the ego, which looks like oncoming traffic. The ego slowed from 7 to 3.3 m/s but didn't stop or move back right, and its front hit the bus (the camera view at impact is smeared). The ego was also rear-ended later.

The route command was RIGHT, but after handoff the ego veered left, ending up about 9 m left of the recorded path near the left curb. Bus 127 swung out of the intersection into those lanes heading toward the ego. The ego slowed from 7.2 to 3.1 m/s but was still in the bus's path, and the two hit front-on at 10.3 s.

After handoff, the ego drifted about 10 m left of the recorded path, which was far to the right for the upcoming RIGHT command, and travelled in the left lanes. It then steered right toward the route and hit bus 127, which was in the adjacent lane and approaching. The ego was braking from 7.5 to 3.6 m/s but too late, and the front contact counts as at fault.

The route said turn RIGHT, but the policy drifted left, off the recorded path (about 10 m off by the end), toward the left lanes. It drove at the city bus (127), which was turning out of the cross street into those lanes, and only began braking late (8.6 to 5.5 m/s). The ego's front hit the bus nearly head-on; the bus was clearly visible in the camera beforehand.

The route command was RIGHT, but the ego steered left across several lanes toward the left curb, ending about 11.6 m from the recorded path, and slowed almost to a stop. Bus 127, in the next lane, came alongside and the ego's side hit it (lateral collision at 11.0 s); a rear contact also happened at some point.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path ran down and to the right through the lanes, but the policy's planned path kept bending left toward the road edge. The ego left the recorded trajectory, slowly crossed the road boundary at about 3–4 m/s and went off-road into the sidewalk and building area at 10.2 s, about 13.5 m from the recorded path. No other actor was involved.

The route command was RIGHT, but after handoff the policy steered left across several lanes, away from the recorded path (7.3 m off by the failure). It drove into bus 127, which was in the far-left lane, and hit it head-on with its front at about 4–5 m/s.

The route command was RIGHT, but after handoff the ego drifted about 8 m left of the recorded path, which stayed in the right-hand lanes, and ended up in the left lanes. There it hit bus 127 front-on as the bus turned in from the intersection and came toward the ego. The ego slowed only gently (9.0 to 6.5 m/s) and never braked hard, even though the bus was clearly visible on camera from 7.3 s.

Although the route command was RIGHT, the ego drifted left, about 7 m off the recorded path, into the lane of bus 127, which was moving slower ahead of it. It kept going at about 7.4 m/s and slowed only to 5.6 m/s, too late, so it hit the back of the bus with its front. The rear contact flagged in the run came after this at-fault front collision.

The route said RIGHT, but the ego drifted left across lanes, ending about 9 m off the recorded path. A bus (127) turned onto the road from the cross street into those left lanes, and the ego braked late (from 8.9 to 5.5 m/s) and hit it head-on. A follower then hit the ego's rear, but only after the front collision.

With a RIGHT command, the ego left its route along the multi-lane road. It steered across the lanes toward the road edge, slowing from 6 to 2.9 m/s, then crossed the curb toward a building wall and sidewalk at about 10.2 s, by then 13.7 m from the human's path. No other actor was involved, and the camera view stayed recognizable before the failure, so the policy's planned path caused it.

The route said turn RIGHT, but the ego drifted left, away from the recorded path (5.4 m off by 8.2 s and 9.4 m off at the failure), into the lanes used by bus 127, which was coming toward it. The ego slowed from 7.4 to 3.0 m/s but still hit the bus head-on at 10.2 s. The camera smearing came after the drift had started, so it is a result of the drift, not the cause.

The route said RIGHT, but the ego drifted left of the recorded path, ending about 6.4 m off it. It steered into the next lane over and hit oncoming bus 127 front-first at about 7 m/s as the bus passed, slowing only slightly before contact.

The command was RIGHT, but after handoff the ego drifted about 9 m left of the recorded human path, and its planned path kept bending further left. Bus 127, which replays its recorded motion, made a turn from the intersection into the lane the ego now occupied and came toward it. The ego slowed from 7.4 to 3.5 m/s but hit the bus head-on. The bus did not react to the ego, but the collision only happened because the policy drove into a lane the real car never used.

The route said RIGHT, but the ego drifted left, about 7 m off the recorded human path, into the left lane. A bus (127) was turning out of the intersection into that same lane and coming toward the ego. The ego slowed only gradually, from 10 to 6.4 m/s, and its front hit the bus head-on.
